text:
naomi: escalating a customer-reported 401s on Dedicated in their VPC after an SSO token rotation. customer says requests that used to succeed with API keys now get 401s. they pasted curl output and traces. I reproduced a failing curl against their dedicated hostname.

naomi: curl they sent:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhb..." \n  https://dedicated-acme.internal/v1/generate
* Connected to dedicated-acme.internal (10.0.2.5) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: dedicated-acme.internal
> Authorization: Bearer eyJhb...
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: 7f3a...
< content-length: 63
{
  "error": "unauthorized",
  "message": "invalid token"
}
```

raj: do we know where the token is being terminated? LB or istio ext_authz?

naomi: customer uses a managed nginx LB in front of istio-ingressgateway. they said they rotated their SSO OIDC keys and also enabled an SSO sidecar on the LB for SSO cookies. our logs at the dedicated edge show requests arriving without `Authorization` but with `Proxy-Authorization`. looks like LB is doing auth termination then forwarding a different header.

luke: can you tcpdump on the ingress pod so we can see what gets to envoy vs what the LB sent? quick check: run `tcpdump -A -s 0 port 443 and host 10.0.2.5` on the customer's ingress (or ask them to run). typical symptom: nginx `auth_request` or `auth_proxy` modules strip Authorization and set `Proxy-Authorization`.

naomi: got a snippet from their tcpdump (trimmed):
```
GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: dedicated-acme.internal
User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
Proxy-Authorization: Basic aGFuZGVzaWdu
X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.23

# note: no Authorization header present at this point
```

raj: yep that's the pattern. Istio/ext_authz or the LB auth module is terminating the original `Authorization` and substituting. By default envoy/istio won't automatically copy `Proxy-Authorization` -> `Authorization`. We need either: 1) change the customer's LB to forward the original header (recommended), or 2) add a header mapping at ingress to restore it.

maria: short-term workaround we can offer: have the customer add an envoy header_to_add rule on the istio-ingressgateway that maps `Proxy-Authorization` back to `Authorization`. example snippet for a VirtualService/EnvoyFilter (customer-managed):
```
# EnvoyFilter fragment (pseudo)
patch: |
  - apply_to: NETWORK_FILTER
    match: ...
    patch: 
      operation: MERGE
      value:
        typed_config:
          '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_metadata.v3.Config
          request_rules:
          - header: "Proxy-Authorization"
            on_header_present:
              metadata_namespace: envoy.lb
              key: x_recovered_auth
```

# then add a route header transform to set Authorization from x_recovered_auth
```

maria: simpler (and safe) curl test we gave them: replicate mapping locally:
```
curl -v -H "Proxy-Authorization: Bearer BADTOKEN" \n  -H "x-test-proxy: 1" \n  https://dedicated-acme.internal/v1/generate
```
if that returns 401 but our envoy mapping returns 200 after mapping, we confirm it's header loss at the LB.

raj: long-term we should update our Dedicated onboarding docs to call out LB auth proxies that terminate auth and the recommended header passthrough or mapping. also add a healthcheck that alerts when Authorization header is absent but Proxy-Authorization present.

naomi: customer is asking whether they need to rotate API keys again. answer: no — if we restore the incoming Authorization header mapping they should be fine. the only real risk is if their SSO replaced token signing keys and OIDC issued tokens are invalid — but customer used API keys originally which should be unaffected. we asked them to send the `x-request-id` from our logs and we can trace.

luke: owners/action items:
- naomi -> confirm LB config with customer and request passthrough for Authorization or to add `auth_request_set` to copy header into `X-Forwarded-Authorization`
- maria -> prepare EnvoyFilter example and rollback-safe snippet we can paste in support ticket
- raj -> add doc blurb to Dedicated runbook + create a small checker to surface missing Authorization headers in console

naomi: created support ticket #TICK-5421 and sent the EnvoyFilter example. pinging @maria for the snippet to paste into the customer ticket. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident created: TICK-5421 | priority P2 | assigned: naomi | link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/TICK-5421

naomi: thanks team — I'll keep this thread updated with customer responses and confirm when they flip the LB setting.
